subject: Engineering Mathematics
summary: first-order ODEs (separable, linear, exact, Bernoulli), higher-order linear ODEs with constant coefficients, complementary function and particular integral, the Euler–Cauchy equation, Laplace transforms and their use in initial-value problems, and the heat, wave and Laplace equations

questions.text: The differential equation whose general solution is y = A cos 3x + B sin 3x (A, B arbitrary constants) is
solution: Concept: Two arbitrary constants → eliminate them by differentiating twice; the result is a 2nd-order ODE.
y′ = −3A sin 3x + 3B cos 3x, y″ = −9A cos 3x − 9B sin 3x = −9y
Exam tip: Number of arbitrary constants = order of the ODE of the family.

questions.text: If dy/dx = xy and y(0) = 1, then y(2) (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Variables separable: dy/y = x dx.
ln y = x²/2 + C; y(0) = 1 gives C = 0, so y = e<sup>x²/2</sup>
Exam tip: Always apply the initial condition before substituting the final x.

questions.text: The solution of x dy/dx + 2y = x² (x > 0) with y(1) = 1 is evaluated at x = 2. The value of y(2) (round off to four decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Write in standard linear form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) before finding the integrating factor.
dy/dx + (2/x)y = x, so IF = e<sup>∫2/x dx</sup> = x²
d(x²y)/dx = x³ → x²y = x⁴/4 + C; y(1) = 1 gives C = 3/4
Exam tip: Divide by the coefficient of dy/dx first; using P = 2 instead of 2/x is the classic slip.

questions.text: The general solution of y″ + 6y′ + 9y = 0 is
solution: Concept: Auxiliary equation m² + 6m + 9 = 0 → (m + 3)² = 0, a repeated root m = −3.
For a repeated root the second solution is x emx: y = (A + Bx)e−3x.
In a spring–mass–damper this is the critically damped case (ζ = 1).
Exam tip: Repeated root → multiply by x; complex roots α ± iβ → eαx(A cos βx + B sin βx).

questions.text: The solution of y″ − y = 0 with y(0) = 0 and y′(0) = 2, evaluated at x = 1 (round off to three decimal places), is ______
solution: Concept: m² − 1 = 0 → m = ±1, so y = Aex + Be−x.
y = e<sup>x</sup> − e<sup>−x</sup> = 2 sinh x
Exam tip: With y(0) = 0, the hyperbolic form (sinh) is quicker than solving for A and B.

questions.text: A particular integral of y″ + 4y = sin 2x is
solution: Concept: sin 2x is already a solution of the homogeneous equation (roots ±2i) — this is resonance, so multiply the trial by x.
Using 1/(D² + a²) sin ax = −(x/2a) cos ax with a = 2:
yp = −(x/4) cos 2x (check: substitution gives sin 2x ✓)
Exam tip: Resonant forcing makes the amplitude grow linearly with time — the reason operating near natural frequency is dangerous.

questions.text: For the Euler–Cauchy equation x²y″ + xy′ − 4y = 0 with y(1) = 2 and y′(1) = 0, the value of y(2) is ______
solution: Concept: Substitute y = xm: m(m − 1) + m − 4 = 0 → m² = 4 → m = ±2.
Exam tip: For Euler–Cauchy the auxiliary equation is m(m − 1) + am + b = 0, not m² + am + b = 0.

questions.text: The Laplace transform of t sin t is
solution: Concept: Multiplication by t: L{t f(t)} = −dF/ds.
Exam tip: Each extra factor of t means one more derivative with respect to s, with a sign of (−1).

questions.text: Using Laplace transforms, solve y′ + 3y = e<sup>−t</sup> with y(0) = 0. The value of y at t = 1 (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: L{y′} = sY − y(0); transform, solve for Y(s), then use partial fractions.
y(t) = ½(e<sup>−t</sup> − e<sup>−3t</sup>)
Exam tip: Check y(0) = 0 from your answer before moving on.

questions.text: If F(s) = (3s + 1)/(s² + 2s + 5) is the Laplace transform of f(t), then f(0<sup>+</sup>) is
solution: Concept: Initial value theorem: f(0+) = lims→∞ sF(s).
sF(s) = (3s² + s)/(s² + 2s + 5) → 3 as s → ∞
f(0+) = 3. (Check: f = e−t(3 cos 2t − sin 2t), f(0) = 3 ✓)
Exam tip: Initial value: s → ∞. Final value: s → 0, and only if all poles of sF(s) are in the left half-plane.

questions.text: The partial differential equation u<sub>xx</sub> + 2u<sub>xy</sub> + 5u<sub>yy</sub> = 0 is
opts: none of these, since it has a mixed term
solution: Concept: For Auxx + Buxy + Cuyy: B² − 4AC < 0 elliptic, = 0 parabolic, > 0 hyperbolic.
B² − 4AC = 4 − 20 = −16 < 0 → elliptic
Exam tip: Laplace equation: elliptic; heat equation: parabolic; wave equation: hyperbolic. Here B is the full coefficient of uxy (not B/2).

questions.text: The 2 kg block shown is attached to a spring of stiffness 800 N/m on a smooth floor. It is pulled 10 mm to the right and released from rest, so that 2ẍ + 800x = 0, x(0) = 0.01 m, ẋ(0) = 0. The time at which the block first passes through the equilibrium position (in s, round off to four decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: ẍ + ω²x = 0 with ω = √(k/m).
First zero when 20t = π/2 → t = π/40 = 0.0785 s (a quarter period)
Exam tip: Released from rest at an extreme, the block reaches equilibrium after T/4, whatever the amplitude.

questions.text: The general solution of (y cos x + 2x e<sup>y</sup>) dx + (sin x + x²e<sup>y</sup> + 2) dy = 0 is
solution: Concept: Check exactness: ∂M/∂y = cos x + 2x ey = ∂N/∂x ✓
Integrate M with respect to x: y sin x + x²e<sup>y</sup>; add the terms of N free of x: 2y
Solution: y sin x + x²ey + 2y = C
Exam tip: After integrating M, add only those terms of N that do not contain x.

questions.text: A rod of unit length, shown in the figure, obeys u<sub>t</sub> = u<sub>xx</sub> with u(0, t) = u(1, t) = 0 and u(x, 0) = sin πx. The temperature at the mid-point x = 0.5 at t = 0.1 (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Separation of variables gives modes sin(nπx) e−n²π²t; the initial profile contains only n = 1.
u(x, t) = sin(πx) e<sup>−π²t</sup>
Exam tip: Higher modes decay as n², so after a short time only the first mode matters.

questions.text: The Bernoulli equation dy/dx + y = y² is reduced to a linear equation by the substitution v = 1/y. The resulting equation is
solution: Concept: For dy/dx + Py = Qyn, put v = y1−n; here n = 2, so v = 1/y.
dv/dx = −y<sup>−2</sup> dy/dx. Divide the ODE by y²: y<sup>−2</sup>dy/dx + y<sup>−1</sup> = 1 → −dv/dx + v = 1
So dv/dx − v = −1 (solution v = 1 + Cex, i.e. y = 1/(1 + Cex)).
Exam tip: Watch the sign that comes from differentiating 1/y.
